subject: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist / egress / DNS / mTLS - integration follow-up

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sana Patel <sana.patel@finpay.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + next steps from today's integration call

Hi Alex / Sana,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary:
- FinPay is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing chat & document summarization (high QPS during batch jobs; low-latency interactive flows).
- Top integration constraints: VPC-based private connectivity (no public egress for inference), IP allowlist for control plane callbacks, DNS resolution inside FinPay network, and mTLS for service-to-service auth where possible.

Technical asks we discussed:
1) VPC endpoints / private connectivity model (VPC peering vs. VPC endpoints + NAT egress).
2) IP allowlist for control plane callbacks and webhook routing (we can provide ranges).
3) TLS/mTLS support between FinPay edge and Redwood connectors; client certs vs. mutual TLS using their gateway.
4) DNS / egress for embeddings and external model access (some of your infra restricts outbound DNS to internal resolvers).
5) SDK auth — preference is to rotate short-lived certs vs. static API key for private deployment.

Proposed next steps:
- I can loop in our integration engineers to map the architecture and share the integration checklist + IP template (see attachments).
- Can we get access to a low-priv test VPC or the IP ranges and DNS constraints by EOD Thu so we can draft the recommended architecture?
- Schedule a deep-dive engineering call — I propose Wed 4/7 at 10am PT.

I will follow up with our engineers (marissa, jonas) and share the checklist.

Best,
Lauren

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today's integration call

Thanks Lauren — good summary. Confirming the ask and adding a few details from our side:

- We cannot allow public egress from our inference VPCs. All outbound must go through a managed NAT/proxy with internal DNS.
- We will publish an IP allowlist for inbound control plane callbacks; prefer a stable set of IPs for firewall rules.
- mTLS is enforced on our side between service endpoints. We can support either client certs (we manage CA) or front with our gateway which does mTLS termination.
- For SDK auth, we prefer short-lived certs (e.g., SPIFFE/SVID flow) but can use a scoped API key during POC if certificate rotation is not supported out-of-the-box.

Next actions from FinPay:
1) I'll share our network constraints doc and an initial IP ranges CSV by EOD Thu (attached to my reply).
2) Please have your engineers propose a recommended topology (VPC Endpoint vs NAT egress path) and list of required firewall rules and DNS entries.

Also please include notes on embeddings and reranker storage: we want to understand how embeddings are stored (encrypted at rest), whether we can host vector index in our VPC, and network patterns for embedding calls/batches.

Thanks,
Alex

Marissa / Jonas — looping you both in on FinPay (prospect RF-2345). They need a private connectivity plan for POC: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist, DNS restrictions, and mTLS options. See the thread below for context and the attached FinPay IP template.

Key POC constraints:
- No public egress from their inference VPCs.
- They want a stable set of IPs for control plane callbacks.
- mTLS or gateway-based mTLS termination; prefer client cert rotation if feasible.
- Want to host vector index inside their VPC if possible (we should outline options and tradeoffs).

Ask: Can you draft a 1-page architecture diagram + runbook describing:
- Two integration options: 1) VPC Endpoint (private link) directly to Redwood connector (recommended for max isolation); 2) NAT egress with strict IP allowlist for callbacks (simpler for POC).
- Required firewall rules and DNS entries for each option.
- Auth options: API key vs short-lived certs vs mTLS via gateway, and what work is needed on our side for each.
- Implications for embeddings/reranker storage and KV cache (hosting index in their VPC vs Redwood-hosted).

Timeline: pickup draft by EOD Fri so we can share with Alex and schedule an engineering call Thursday 4/8 or Friday 4/9.

Hi all — draft architecture and runbook notes below. Attaching a concise checklist PDF. Happy to walk through live.

Short answer (recommendation):
- For POC: use a PrivateLink / VPC Endpoint connecting FinPay VPC to a Redwood connector in a customer-dedicated layer (no public IPs). This gives strongest isolation and avoids public egress constraints.
- If PrivateLink not available immediately, a controlled NAT egress configuration with a fixed egress IP range can work for short-term POC, but increases attack surface and requires stricter proxy/DNS handling.

High-level items (PrivateLink path):
- Network:
  - Set up a VPC Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) from FinPay app VPC to Redwood ingress endpoint.
  - No public egress required; DNS configured to resolve internal endpoint via provided Route53 private hosted zone or via CNAME to endpoint inside their resolver.
  - Control plane callbacks originate from a small, stable set of IPs (we'll reserve a /29 for POC).
- Auth:
  - Option A (recommended): mTLS using client certs issued by FinPay's CA. Redwood connector will verify client certs; we support cert rotation via ACME-like automation or manual rotation for POC.
  - Option B: short-lived tokens (JWT) issued by FinPay's OIDC provider exchanged for session tokens at Redwood. Requires OIDC integration (we can accept OIDC claims + audience).
  - Option C (fallback): scoped API keys stored in an encrypted secret store; rotate keys frequently.
- Embeddings / rerankers:
  - Hosting vector index inside FinPay VPC: we can deploy a lightweight indexer as part of the connector stack that stores vectors locally; Redwood can call it over the private link for reranking/nearest-neighbor lookups.
  - Redwood-hosted index: simpler for initial POC (we keep vectors encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys), but requires controlled egress from FinPay for upload and retrieval.
- DNS / egress:
  - If FinPay blocks public DNS, we recommend configuring Route53 private hosted zone forwarded to Redwood endpoint and resolving via internal resolver.
  - For NAT path, ensure the egress NAT IPs are whitelisted on Redwood control plane and that DNS allows resolution for helm chart/cloud endpoints.

Runbook & checklist (attached):
- Provide FinPay with: IP template (attached), required firewall rules, expected cert subject names, and sample envoy config for mTLS termination at the gateway.
- Schedule: 1) POC network setup (1-2 days), 2) connector deploy + cert exchange (1 day), 3) validation + load test (1 day).

Links:
- PrivateLink setup guide: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBbCdEfGhVpc-integration-playbook
- Sample envoy mTLS config: https://drive.google.com/open?id=envoy-mtls-sample

Next steps:
- Lauren: please confirm POC window and a time for a deep-dive with FinPay network/security.
- Alex: can you confirm whether FinPay wants connector-managed cert validation (we supply CA bundle) or to terminate at your gateway?

I can join Thu 4/8 10am PT for the call. Attaching "redwood-vpc-integration-checklist.pdf".
